scope.description: Exact published OSCP refresh lead covering NavigationGate, the MK2 inertial-sensor family, Montréal operations, federal testing and supplier paths, public funding and bounded readiness evidence.

source.title: NavigationGate
source.locator: Architecture, interfaces, onboard GNSS and aiding inputs
source.summary: NavigationGate is presented as a distinct inertial-navigation processing unit that pairs with OSCP IMUs and combines onboard sensor fusion, dual-antenna RTK-compatible GNSS, external aiding, storage and vehicle interfaces.

leads.evidenceLocator: NavigationGate and MK2 official product pages, public technical documentation, CanadaBuys contract histories, NRC project records, NGen reporting and representative patent evidence
followUpQuestions: What drift, latency, update-rate and aiding-loss performance has NavigationGate demonstrated for the exact IMU and vehicle configuration under consideration?
Which environmental, electromagnetic, safety and cybersecurity qualifications apply to the shipping NavigationGate and MK2 configuration?
What production capacity, component-origin controls, lead time and support package apply beyond the limited first NavigationGate batch?
Which testing, additional-sales or Defence Drone Initiative opportunity is tied to a specific OSCP configuration, and what buyer acceptance evidence exists?
reviewWarnings: NavigationGate was offered through a limited first-production-batch preorder on September 1, 2026; no reviewed public source establishes shipment, customer acceptance or operational deployment.

No public NavigationGate manual, message schema, configuration API, weight, power, latency, GNSS-band specification, environmental qualification, cybersecurity assessment or independent product test was found.
OSCP's January 2026 road comparison predates NavigationGate and did not use its Kalman filter; it must not be presented as NavigationGate performance evidence.
The Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace record is a nominal-value supplier-pool supply arrangement, not an order, task authorization, revenue event, product-specific award or deployment.

The Innovative Solutions Canada Testing Stream contract supports bounded testing; the public record does not establish fielding, delivery acceptance or that NavigationGate is the tested configuration.
OSCP sources conflict on founding year: the current About page says 2019, the September 2026 release says 2015, and an earlier LinkedIn profile said 2016; founded_year remains unchanged.
MK2E2 and MK2Z public specifications are labelled preliminary, and environmental or ingress-protection status remains in process for some configurations.
OSCP's ITAR-free statement is a company claim and does not remove the need for configuration-specific export-control and component-origin review.

A March 17, 2026 Quebec registry non-conformity notice is a dated administrative notice, not proof that the company is inactive; later federal awards continued and current registry status remains unresolved.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: OSCP's current About and Contact pages resolved the legal operating identity, Montréal footprint, leadership, fabless model and public inquiry channels.
The NavigationGate product page resolved the processor, sensor-fusion, GNSS, aiding, storage and interface architecture, while the INS documentation index remained incomplete.
The MK2 documentation resolved serial and CAN-FD frames and output-rate limits; it added no public NavigationGate manual, latency or performance envelope.
The Quebec registry lane found a dated non-conformity notice but no live status profile; later federal awards prevented an unsupported inactive-company conclusion.
Representative patent-family review confirmed OSCPS optical-gyroscope filings and a Canadian grant publication without treating patent status as performance or deployment evidence.
CanadaBuys resolved the Testing Stream contract value and term, while the public record did not name NavigationGate or establish fielding and acceptance.
CanadaBuys resolved the DDI Marketplace supply arrangement as supplier-pool qualification and found no task authorization, order, revenue or deployment.
NRC records resolved the NAVPIC, PIC-IMU and defence-readiness contribution amounts and terms while leaving partner identity, completed outcomes and operational use unresolved.
NGen resolved the OSCP-led photonic-wirebonding consortium and investment basis, but the report did not establish production output, sales or customer delivery.
The final dated and bilingual-name sweep confirmed the September 1 launch and legal operating identity but left founding year, current registry status and named customers unresolved.

leads.refreshSummary: OSCPS Motion Sensing is proposed to replace the generic capability with the MK2 family, add the NavigationGate capability, and record the 2026-09-01 launch plus bounded Testing Stream and DDI pathways.
intendedChanges: Update public identity, commercial status, contact, current activity, operating context, Canadian footprint and executive decision fields.
Replace the generic low-SWaP-C capability with the configuration-bounded MK2 family and add NavigationGate as a separate aided inertial-navigation processor.
Add three federal program participations and four separately based public funding events without converting testing or supplier eligibility into deployment.
